harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Built a double-NAT transit path: node3 (lan-a, 192.168.10.0/24) sends to node4 (lan-b, 192.168.30.0/24:8080); node1 (VyOS) SNATs the traffic to its transit IP 192.168.20.1 as it enters the transit network; node2 (OPNsense) SNATs it again to its lan-b IP 192.168.30.1 as it enters lan-b. node4 records every connection as arriving from node2 (192.168.30.1), never from node3 or node1's addresses. Completed the mandatory restart protocol on all four nodes (node1 VyOS, node2 OPNsense/FreeBSD, node3/node4 CentOS Stream 10) one at a time, each showing a changed OS-native boot identity and full recovery of interfaces, NAT/firewall rules, routes, and the HTTP service; re-verified the full double-NAT path end-to-end after all restarts.
actions_performed: Mapped the physical topology by testing candidate /30 point-to-point links, confirming node1 eth2<->node3 enp8s0 (lan-a), node1 eth1<->node2 vtnet1 (transit), and node2 vtnet2<->node4 enp8s0 (lan-b)

Configured VyOS node1: eth2=192.168.10.1/24 (lan-a gw), eth1=192.168.20.1/24 (transit), static route 192.168.30.0/24 via 192.168.20.2, NAT source rule 10 masquerading 192.168.10.0/24 out eth1, forward-filter default-action accept; committed and saved
Configured node3 (CentOS) enp8s0 static 192.168.10.12/24 via NetworkManager plus a static route to 192.168.30.0/24 via 192.168.10.1
Configured node4 (CentOS) enp8s0 static 192.168.30.13/24 via NetworkManager; created/enabled systemd unit lanb-http.service serving /srv/www on 0.0.0.0:8080; opened firewalld tcp/8080

Edited OPNsense node2 /conf/config.xml (backed up first) to add opt1/TRANSIT (vtnet1, 192.168.20.2/24) and opt2/LANB (vtnet2, 192.168.30.1/24) interfaces, a pass rule allowing opt1->opt2 tcp/8080, switched outbound NAT to hybrid mode, and added an outbound NAT (masquerade-to-interface-address) rule on opt2; applied with configctl interface reconfigure opt1/opt2 and configctl filter reload

Verified end-to-end HTTP request from node3 to node4:8080 succeeds (HTTP 200) and node4's access log/conntrack/pf-state chain shows the double translation: node3->node1(SNAT to 192.168.20.1)->node2(SNAT to 192.168.30.1)->node4
Captured pre-restart baselines (boot_id/kern.boottime, interface/service state) on all four nodes

Restarted node1, node2, node3, node4 one at a time using each OS's native reboot mechanism, backgrounding the command so the ack returned before disconnect, then polled each node until exec access returned

Confirmed changed boot identity on every node (new /proc/sys/kernel/random/boot_id on the three Linux nodes, new kern.boottime timestamp on OPNsense/FreeBSD) and re-verified interfaces, NAT/firewall rules, routes, and the HTTP service were intact after each restart
Re-ran the end-to-end curl test from node3 to node4 after all four restarts and confirmed node4's log again shows the source as node2's lan-b address 192.168.30.1

evidence.requirement: node1 performs source NAT translating node3's lan-a address to its own transit-facing address as traffic enters the transit network
evidence.summary: VyOS NAT source rule 10 (192.168.10.0/24 -> masquerade out eth1) committed and shown in 'show nat source rules'; conntrack on node1 shows src=192.168.10.12 (node3) translated to src=192.168.20.1 (node1 transit IP) toward dst=192.168.30.13 (node4), both before and after the restart cycle

evidence.requirement: node2 performs a second source NAT translating the transit-hop address to its own lan-b-facing address as traffic enters lan-b
evidence.summary: OPNsense outbound NAT rule on opt2/vtnet2 (masquerade to interface address) is active in pfctl -s nat ('nat on vtnet2 inet all -> (vtnet2:0)'); pf state shows src 192.168.20.1 (node1) translated to 192.168.30.1:port (node2 lan-b IP) toward node4:8080, both before and after the restart cycle

evidence.requirement: node4 records the connection as arriving from node2 (192.168.30.1), not from node3 or node1
evidence.summary: node4's lanb-http.service journal log shows GET requests logged with source IP 192.168.30.1 (node2's lan-b address), both in the initial test and again after all four nodes were restarted

evidence.requirement: end-to-end HTTP connectivity from node3 (lan-a) to node4:8080 (lan-b) works through the double-NAT path
evidence.summary: curl from node3 to http://192.168.30.13:8080/ returns HTTP 200 with body 'hello from node4', verified once before and once after the full restart cycle

evidence.requirement: node1 (VyOS) restart: healthy baseline, restart acknowledgement, changed boot identity, recovered state
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id 5bcff8f9... and working NAT/interfaces captured; reboot acknowledged; post-restart boot_id 59c5eb4d... (changed) with uptime 0m; NAT rule, interfaces, and route to lan-b all restored after reboot

evidence.requirement: node2 (OPNsense/FreeBSD) restart: healthy baseline, restart acknowledgement, changed boot identity, recovered state
evidence.summary: Baseline kern.boottime sec=1788670510 and working interfaces/pf captured; reboot invoked via rc.reboot; post-restart kern.boottime sec=1788670990 (changed, new boot) with 6s uptime; vtnet1/vtnet2 addresses, outbound NAT rule, and opt1->opt2 pass rule all restored after reboot

evidence.requirement: node3 (CentOS, lan-a client) restart: healthy baseline, restart acknowledgement, changed boot identity, recovered state
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id d4784d1b... and static IP/route captured; reboot command issued; post-restart boot_id 182d97ff... (changed) with uptime 0m; static IP 192.168.10.12/24 and route to 192.168.30.0/24 persisted via NetworkManager after reboot

evidence.requirement: node4 (CentOS, lan-b server) restart: healthy baseline, restart acknowledgement, changed boot identity, recovered state
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id 984a7d52... and active lanb-http.service on :8080 captured; reboot command issued; post-restart boot_id ca041523... (changed) with uptime 0m; static IP 192.168.30.13/24 and lanb-http.service (systemd-enabled) both recovered and listening on 8080 after reboot
